title: Storage that refuses to become a coordinator
subtitle: A tensor store that appends, returns a stable address and knows nothing about its consumers; the coordinator tables it once had were removed and the boundary is enforced by checks in the build
technologies: Idempotency, exactly-once effects and crash recovery

stats.label: refusals the build checks for in the source
lines of acceptance test holding the contract

lede: The vector store under my research pipeline receives tensors from the extraction engines and the embedders and hands back an address. For a while it also tracked which consumers had accepted which payloads, de-duplicated by content, and answered questions about consumer schemas, because each of those was convenient for someone. I took them out and wrote the boundary down. A producer sends an envelope. The store parses the envelope, recomputes the content hash over the tensor bytes, and checks the envelope's characteristics against the current generation; any mismatch is a hard reject. It writes a journal entry first, then the payload and the identifier, then a lineage row in the database, and the call returns a reference.
quote: Every one of them made the store a coordinator, and a coordinator is a single point of contention and a second source of truth.
evidence: Append-only log design: a tensor store that journals each append before payload and lineage and returns a stable address of generation, shard, row, offset and content hash.
System boundary design: coordinator duties removed from a storage service, with 4 refusals enforced by build checks that fail if the forbidden patterns reappear.
Exactly-once delivery and crash recovery: shards replayed and truncated to the last consistent journal entry before the listener binds, with torn tails counted in a metric.
Backpressure and admission control: a high-water mark answering busy with a retry hint and a client circuit breaker with a half-open probe, held by an acceptance test of about 800 lines.
author: Corey James
